target.title: fix(microsoft): add timeout to voices list request
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Microsoft voice discovery could wait indefinitely when the voices endpoint accepted the HTTP connection but never returned a response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Microsoft provider already has timeout-aware synthesis behavior, but `listMicrosoftVoices` did not pass a deadline into its guarded voices-list request. This change adds a bounded default timeout for voice discovery while preserving existing request headers, SSRF policy, debug proxy capture, and response parsing.

## User Impact

A stalled Microsoft voices endpoint no longer blocks voice discovery forever. The discovery request now fails boundedly instead of leaving callers pending.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/microsoft/speech-provider.test.ts` - passed; `Test Files  1 passed (1)`, `Tests  12 passed (12)`.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/microsoft/speech-provider.ts extensions/microsoft/speech-provider.test.ts` - passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/microsoft/speech-provider.ts extensions/microsoft/speech-provider.test.ts` - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD` - passed; exit 0.
- Open PR collision check: searched open PR topics and scanned the latest 500 open PR changed-file lists; no open PR touched `extensions/microsoft/speech-provider.ts`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Microsoft voices-list GETs now have a deadline when the remote endpoint accepts the request but never sends a response.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; real `node:http` loopback server that receives the `listMicrosoftVoices` request and deliberately never responds.

Exact command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/microsoft/speech-provider.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: the focused regression drives the exported `listMicrosoftVoices` path, redirects fetch to the local hanging server, asserts the server receives one request, and observes a `TimeoutError` within the bounded window.

What was not tested: live Microsoft/Bing voice-list traffic; the hang is reproduced with a real local HTTP server, not the real third-party service.
